prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable ledger traces donations to verified outcomes, so the Main KPI of 500,000,000 donations traced to outcomes is unmet. The best-known outcome estimates are model-based, not traced: GiveWell builds program-level cost-effectiveness models (top charities roughly 3,500 to 5,500 US dollars per life saved on 2021 figures) with external-validity adjustments and subjective moral weights, notes a past estimate about 100 times off, and does not link a specific donor's dollar to a specific result (https://www.givewell.org/how-we-work/our-criteria/cost-effectiveness). A 2025 evidence gap map of results-based payments shows uneven evidence (https://doi.org/10.1057/s41287-025-00713-9), aid-data governance stays fragmented across regimes such as IATI (https://doi.org/10.17645/pag.10508), and blockchain donation-tracking designs are proposals that trace money, not impact (https://doi.org/10.1002/sd.3260). GitHub holds two small donation-tracking projects. Honest limit: tracing financial flows (IATI publishing, blockchain ledgers, outcome-based contracts) is known and is not new work; the unsolved part is causal attribution of outcomes to marginal dollars with verification, so tasks must target a checkable piece such as a verifiable outcome-attestation protocol tested on real programme data.
